problem: Zero-shot MLLM-based VLN agents in continuous environments decide from the current view and a textual action history only, so they drift off course, get distracted by irrelevant objects, misjudge progress and stop prematurely.
motivation: VLN-CE instructions span many steps while MLLMs have limited context, and small heading or position errors compound in continuous space. Agents need global route context plus a way to detect and recover from mistakes without supervision.
key_idea: A frozen MLLM alternates global-local-global reasoning (look forward: decompose instruction into sub-goals and landmarks; look now: pick a waypoint for the active sub-goal; look backward: audit the executed trajectory and decide stay/continue/backtrack/look-around).
insight: Ablation on R2R-CE shows both global planning and trajectory audit matter: local-only gives SR 20, adding look-forward gives SR 28, and adding look-backward gives SR 34 (NE 6.55 -> 6.22 -> 5.87). Backbone quality also matters (GPT-5 SR 34 vs GPT-4o 28 vs GPT-4v 26), though the structure helps across all of them.
method: Look forward: prompted with the instruction and initial panorama, the MLLM splits the instruction into atomic sub-instructions at spatial connectives and pairs each with a salient landmark, forming a coarse global plan.

Look now: a transformer waypoint predictor (as in Open-Nav) proposes candidate viewpoints from panoramic RGB-D; the MLLM gets the active sub-instruction, candidate images and descriptions, and textual history, picks the best waypoint, and outputs an estimated distance to the landmark.
Sub-goal completion trigger: when the estimated landmark distance falls below a threshold, the sub-goal is considered ready for inspection.

Look backward: builds a textual replay of visited viewpoints (landmarks, objects, distances) and asks the MLLM whether the trajectory satisfies each sub-instruction in order and whether any landmark or turn was missed.

Adaptive judge meta-skills: continue (advance to the next sub-goal), stay (re-query at the same pose), backtrack (roll back to the last reliable waypoint and truncate the trajectory), look-around (visit neighbor viewpoints and re-evaluate).
Plug-and-play: purely prompt-based on a frozen MLLM, no gradient updates, usable in other LLM-core VLN pipelines.

setting.backbone: GPT-5 (gpt-5-2025-08-07, frozen) as MLLM planner + pretrained transformer waypoint predictor (from Open-Nav)
setting.action_space: predicted candidate waypoints executed as low-level continuous-environment actions (turn/forward)

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 randomly sampled episodes from English val-unseen

results: On a 100-episode R2R-CE val-unseen subset, Three-Step Nav with GPT-5 reaches SR 34, SPL 29.12, NE 5.87, beating the strongest zero-shot baseline SmartWay (SR 29, SPL 22.46) and Open-Nav on NE (6.70). On a 100-episode RxR-CE subset it gets SR 22.0, SPL 16.1, NE 9.21, best NE/nDTW/SPL among zero-shot methods but SR slightly below AO-Planner (22.4).
limitations: Depends on a powerful proprietary MLLM (GPT-5) with high cost and latency; performance drops with GPT-4o/4v
Evaluated only on 100-episode subsets in simulation, with no real robot; still far below supervised methods (e.g. ETPNav SR 52 on R2R-CE, 54.8 on RxR-CE)
No learning from feedback; very long or ambiguous instructions remain hard
